Action: # Public Site: Multiple Author Affiliations
public_site/multiple_author_affiliations
## Author with multiple affiliations is displayed once on the article page

Setup: Open /testdrive/multiple_affiliations in its own tab and keep it open for the whole test - closing or navigating away from it removes the test data. Do all of the steps below in a separate tab.
Setup: At the end of the test use the 'FINISH TESTING AND CLEAN UP' link on the testdrive page, unless you are going on to the other tests in this testset
Open the "article_page" link from the testdrive "links" section

Expected Test Results: The authors line reads "Ana Author, Ben Author, Cat Author" - each author appears exactly once

Action: Click the "Affiliations" button under the authors list

Expected Test Results: The affiliations section expands
"Ana Author" is listed once, followed by an ORCiD link and then "University of Oxford", "Harvard University" and "MIT", each on its own line, in that order
"Ben Author" is listed once with "Sorbonne University"
"Cat Author" is listed with no affiliation and no ORCiD

Action: Click the ORCiD link under "Ana Author"

Expected Test Results: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-2345-6789 opens in a new tab

Action: Use a screen reader or the browser's accessibility inspector on the expanded section

Expected Test Results: Each author is a term (dt) and each of their affiliations is a separate description (dd) belonging to it

Action: ## Upload DOAJ XML where an author references multiple affiliations
Setup: Open /testdrive/multiple_affiliations in its own tab and keep it open (see the first test in this testset)
Setup: Copy the "doaj_xml" value from the testdrive "upload_data" section and save it as a file called multiple_affiliations.xml. It already contains the testdrive journal's ISSNs.
In a separate tab, log in with the testdrive publisher username and password
Open the "publisher_xml_upload" link
Choose "DOAJ Native XML" as the format, select multiple_affiliations.xml and click "Upload"

Expected Test Results: A flash message is shown: "File uploaded and waiting to be processed. Check back here for updates."

Action: Wait a short time and reload the page

Expected Test Results: The upload is shown as "successfully processed" with the note "1 articles imported (1 new, 0 updated)"

Action: Open the "journal_toc" link and click the article titled "XML Multiple Affiliations ..."

Expected Test Results: The authors line reads "Jane Doe, John Smith" - each author appears once

Action: Click the "Affiliations" button

Expected Test Results: "Jane Doe" shows an ORCiD link, then "University of Oxford" and "Harvard University" on separate lines
"John Smith" shows "Harvard University" and "MIT" on separate lines
"Harvard University" is shown under both authors, although it is defined only once in the XML file

Action: ## Create articles with multiple affiliations through the API
Setup: Open /testdrive/multiple_affiliations in its own tab and keep it open (see the first test in this testset)
Setup: You need a tool that can send a POST request with a JSON body, eg curl, Postman, or the API docs page /api/docs
Send a POST request to the "api_create_article" link with header "Content-Type: application/json" and the "api_json_affiliations_list" value as the body

Expected Test Results: The response status is 201 and the response contains the new article's id

Action: Open /article/<the returned id>, then click "Affiliations"

Expected Test Results: "Api Author" is listed once with "Uni One" and "Uni Two" on separate lines

Action: Send a GET request to /api/articles/<the returned id>?api_key=<testdrive publisher api_key>

Expected Test Results: The author in bibjson.author has an "affiliations" list: ["Uni One", "Uni Two"]
There is no "affiliation" (singular) field

Action: Send another POST request in the same way, with the "api_json_legacy_affiliation" value as the body. It uses the old single "affiliation" string field.

Expected Test Results: The response status is 201 - the old field is still accepted

Action: Send a GET request for the second article's id

Expected Test Results: The author has "affiliations": ["Old Style University"], converted from the old field

Action: ## Enter and edit multiple affiliations in the article metadata form
Setup: Open /testdrive/multiple_affiliations in its own tab and keep it open (see the first test in this testset)
Setup: In a separate tab, log in with the testdrive publisher username and password
Open the "publisher_metadata_form" link

Expected Test Results: In the Authors section the field is labelled "Affiliations", with help text telling you to separate multiple affiliations with a semicolon (;)

Action: Enter Article Title "Form Multiple Affiliations", a Full-Text URL such as https://example.com/form-affs, and select the testdrive journal's ISSN
For the first author enter Name "Form Author" and Affiliations "University of Oxford ; Harvard University;;MIT"
Click "Add Article"

Expected Test Results: The message "Article created/updated" is shown

Action: Open the "journal_toc" link, open the "Form Multiple Affiliations" article and click "Affiliations"

Expected Test Results: "Form Author" is listed once with exactly three affiliations: "University of Oxford", "Harvard University" and "MIT" - extra spaces are removed and the empty value between ";;" is ignored

Action: ## Admin edits an article with multiple affiliations
Setup: Open /testdrive/multiple_affiliations in its own tab and keep it open (see the first test in this testset)
Setup: In a separate tab, log in as an admin
Open /admin/article/<testdrive article id>

Expected Test Results: The first author is "Ana Author" and the Affiliations field shows "University of Oxford; Harvard University; MIT"

Action: Change the Affiliations to "University of Oxford; MIT" and save the article

Expected Test Results: The article saves without error

Action: Open the "article_page" link and click "Affiliations"

Expected Test Results: "Ana Author" now shows only "University of Oxford" and "MIT"
The other authors are unchanged

Action: ## OAI-PMH oai_doaj output for an author with multiple affiliations
Setup: Open /testdrive/multiple_affiliations in its own tab and keep it open (see the first test in this testset)
Open /oai.article?verb=GetRecord&metadataPrefix=oai_doaj&identifier=oai:doaj.org/article:<testdrive article id>

Expected Test Results: "Ana Author" appears once in the authors list, with three affiliationId elements
Each of those ids matches an affiliationName in the affiliationsList with the values "University of Oxford", "Harvard University" and "MIT"
